source.title: On the Blessing of Pre-training in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Wei Yao; Zhaoyang Wang; Geng-Ze Xu; Chen Qian; Dong-Rui Liu; Ziqiao Wang; Yong Liu; Yunbei Xu

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether weak-label training can outperform the weak supervisor and how pre-training stage and representations affect that result. The LLM experiments train a linear head on frozen backbones rather than fine-tuning the full model, so this is a conceptual rather than exact reproduction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports W2SG performance trends across checkpoint families and tasks, synthetic weak-label training outcomes, theoretical results, and correlations between representations and W2SG. Values shown only in plots are recorded as figure only. No rows are made for cited results from other work or for landscape quantities that do not report an outcome on W2SG performance.
record.test_reason: The paper trains Pythia-6.9B and OLMo-7B pre-training checkpoints on weak labels and compares them with the weak supervisor on HH-RLHF and CAI-Harmless (V1, V3). It sweeps pre-training alignment, signal strength, supervisor quality and learning rate in a synthetic single-index model (V3). It proves a conditional theorem on when the student lands in a basin that lets it beat the supervisor (V5). The method differs from the original: a linear head on a frozen backbone, no PGR reported, and checkpoint stage varied rather than size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that pre-training is a necessary geometric warm start for W2SG, and that W2SG is not innate but emerges via a phase transition during pre-training, then saturates at a weak-label bias floor. They also report that linear-probe accuracy correlates with W2SG and predicts it better than evaluation loss.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains a linear projection head on frozen pre-training backbones using weak labels, rather than fine-tuning the full strong model. It also studies synthetic spherical-PGD models and checkpoint trajectories.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance depends on pre-training checkpoint, synthetic task alignment, latent signal strength, weak-supervisor quality, learning rate, and fine-tuning duration. Linear-probe and evaluation-loss associations vary by model family and task.
record.problems: LLM performance comparisons are plotted without exact accuracy values or PGR; LLM validation is limited to helpfulness and harmlessness reward modeling; LLM training uses a linear head on frozen backbones rather than full-model fine-tuning. Synthetic results are also largely figure-based. The paper's theoretical guarantee relies on a stylized spiked-Gaussian/PCA model and stated assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out. Figure-only checkpoint trajectories are recorded as aggregate phase-specific rows for each model family and task; exact plotted values are not recoverable from the text.

untested.parts: PGR and strong-ceiling comparison: ceiling models are trained but their accuracies are never reported. Full-model fine-tuning is not done (linear head on frozen backbone). Tasks other than reward modelling are not tested.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss-variant comparison.
No sweep of student or supervisor size; no chess or NLP classification tasks; no cross-task comparison of PGR.
No distribution shift, no exploitation of supervisor blind spots, no weak/strong error-similarity analysis.
Only the spiked-Gaussian single-index model with PCA initialisation and online spherical PGD; no general model classes.
No vision or other non-language modality.

missing.what: Strong-ceiling accuracies: ceilings are trained on ground truth but never reported, so PGR cannot be computed
Empirical effective-basin angle (~49.4°–55.1°) and μ, ϕ values versus the theoretical worst-case radius (0.6°–6.1°)

record.verdict_notes: Synthetic rows are toy single-index simulations and were relinked from V1 to V3/V5. In the LLM rows the weak supervisor is a trained 1B model, so early 7B checkpoints are not clearly 'strong'; the failure phase partly reflects that. Accuracy gains over the weak line look small in the plots and are not stated numerically. The R10 initialisation value is inconsistent between text (ρ=0.4) and figure legend (ρ=0.3).

versions.untested_parts: The LLM results do not report PGR, and the main LLM accuracy values are presented in plots rather than numerically in the text. No numerical comparison to a strong ceiling is given for the checkpoint sweeps.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensemble, or loss-variant comparison is performed.

Tests checkpoint progression, two model families, two reward-modeling tasks, and representation-based predictors. It does not sweep student or supervisor size, test chess, or compare NLP with chess or reward modeling.

No distribution-shift experiment, test of exploiting supervisor-blind errors, or comparison based on weak/strong error similarity. The paper does report regression after excessive synthetic fine-tuning, but does not test the failure modes specified in this version.
Theory is established for the paper's single-index, spiked-Gaussian setting and stated assumptions; no general theorem for arbitrary model classes or tasks is tested.
No vision or other non-language modality experiment.

rows.subject: Randomly initialized strong ceiling model
rows.operation_detail: Spherical PGD on ground-truth labels in the theoretical single-index setting

conditions.value: uniformly random on the unit sphere

rows.measure: Change in squared distance to the ground-truth parameter
rows.value: E[∥wN − v*∥₂²] − ∥w0 − v*∥₂² → 0 with high probability
rows.uncertainty: High probability; no numerical probability stated
rows.note: The authors infer that the randomly initialized model remains uninformative and underperforms the informative weak supervisor, even with true labels.
rows.check: Adapted from Jones-McCormick et al. (Theorem 3.4), not a new result. It concerns a ceiling model trained on ground-truth labels, not a weak-to-strong student. The comparison to the supervisor is the authors' inference.

rows.subject: Pre-trained strong student
rows.stage_stated: initialized by oriented PCA; then trained
rows.operation_detail: Spherical PGD on weak labels from an informative supervisor

conditions.value: single-index model with spiked Gaussian data
Assumptions 3.1 and 3.4, including detectable latent signal, task alignment, bounded supervisor bias, and stable learning rate
oriented PCA initialization inside effective region

rows.measure: Expected squared distance to ground truth after T steps; theoretical W2SG guarantee
rows.baseline: Weak supervisor has nonzero risk; exact numerical risk not stated
rows.value: Theorem 3.5 bounds expected squared distance by a decaying term toward D∞ = 7δG/μ + 2ϕ²/μ², plus Õ(d⁻¹ᐟ²); under the assumptions, the trajectory remains in the effective region with high probability
rows.uncertainty: High-probability and asymptotic bound; no empirical error bar
rows.locator: Theorem 3.5, Section 3.3; proof in Appendix B.6
rows.note: The authors state that this mechanism enables the student to surpass the supervisor, but the bound has a nonzero error floor and holds only under the stated assumptions.
rows.check: A theorem, not an empirical V1 result, so V1 is removed. The bound shows the trajectory stays inside the effective region with error floor D∞. It does not directly prove L(w) < L(v_weak); the authors argue that link qualitatively.

rows.subject: Synthetic strong student
rows.operation_detail: Weak-label fine-tuning for 30 steps
rows.measure: Final distance to ground truth, compared with weak-model error
rows.baseline: Weak-model error; plotted without a stated numerical value
rows.value: Successful W2SG occurs only when pre-training alignment ρ passes a critical threshold; figure values only
rows.note: The text describes a threshold-dependent result but does not give the threshold numerically.
rows.check: Toy single-index model, not a strong/weak model pair, so V1 is removed. For V3 the result is a clear dependence on alignment ρ above a threshold, so the state is observed rather than partial. The threshold value is figure-only.

rows.operation_detail: Weak-label spherical PGD fine-tuning
rows.measure: Distance to ground truth compared with weak-supervisor error
rows.value: Poor initialization prevents the student from surpassing the weak supervisor; it stagnates at or above the supervisor's error floor
rows.locator: Figure 1b and Section 4.1; setup in Appendix C.1
rows.note: The text explicitly describes failure for this initialization.
rows.check: Synthetic toy; V1 removed. Absent refers to beating the supervisor at τ=0.1. This is consistent with the V3 dependence and the V5 prediction.

rows.operation_detail: Continued weak-label fine-tuning

conditions.value: excessive iterations after the initial improvement

rows.measure: Distance to ground truth / generalization relative to weak-supervisor error
rows.baseline: Earlier fine-tuning performance below the weak supervisor's error; exact values not stated

conditions.value: λ below the theoretical detectability threshold

rows.value: PCA fails to extract meaningful features and error remains high; poor alignment also prevents generalization despite detectable signal
rows.note: The text explicitly describes failure below the signal threshold and for poor alignment.

rows.subject: Synthetic strong student
rows.operation_detail: Weak-label fine-tuning while varying intrinsic task alignment
rows.measure: W2SG error relative to weak-model error
rows.value: With adequate signal, error decreases as ρ increases and eventually falls below the weak-supervisor baseline; with λ = 0.05, error remains catastrophic at approximately 1.41
rows.note: Outcome depends on both pre-training alignment and signal strength.
rows.check: Synthetic toy; V1 removed. The ρ-dependence with adequate signal, and failure at λ=0.05 (error ≈1.41), match the stated assumptions.

rows.subject: Synthetic strong student
rows.operation_detail: Weak-label fine-tuning while varying weak-supervisor quality
rows.measure: W2SG error and whether it falls below weak-supervisor baseline
rows.value: Error decreases as γ increases; well-pre-trained models cross below the weak baseline, while poorly pre-trained models may fail even with a competent supervisor
rows.note: The result varies with both supervisor quality and pre-training alignment.
rows.check: Synthetic toy; V1 removed. Error falls with supervisor quality γ, and pre-training quality gates success, as described.

rows.subject: Synthetic strong student

rows.operation_detail: Weak-label fine-tuning while varying learning rate
rows.measure: W2SG error relative to weak-model baseline
rows.value: All tested initializations enter the W2SG success zone in the reported learning-rate sweet spot
rows.note: The text says even the poor-initialization model falls below the weak baseline in this range.
rows.check: Synthetic toy; V1 removed. The 'Poor Init' model, whose initial error exceeds the weak baseline, also beats the supervisor in the learning-rate sweet spot. relationships.condition: Optimisation choices (learning rate, training duration) and choice of predictor metric
